_comment: A map recipe (#331, decision 0010): the land before anything is placed on it. size: the square map's side in metres, centred on the origin. relief: metres from the lowest to the highest the noise reaches. hill_mask: a slow noise (frequency, 1 / metres) whose value between from and to fades hilly country in; outside it lies near-flat lowland. layers: noise summed for the height, each with frequency, amplitude (share of relief), octaves, and masked (only where the hill mask says hilly, and only rising out of the lowland). walkable: max_grade (rise per metre a player still walks easily), min_share (the least share of the map that gentle), flat_grade and min_flat_share (near-flat ground for towns and fields, and how much of it the map needs), hillside_grade and min_hillside_share (real hillsides: the least share of the map that rises at least this much); the tests hold every seed to these. water: ponds where water would collect: the land is surveyed every cell metres, a basin at least min_depth deep and min_area square metres becomes a pond (shrunk to max_area by lowering its level), its level freeboard metres below where it would spill, its bed deepen times deeper than the land.
